title: Birth in Oakland, Mississippi, and his musical brothers
summary: Born 1907; mother a concert pianist, father a country fiddler; brother Johnny with the Arcadian Serenaders, brother Dick the harmonica champion, then school and marriage.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well. I thought I'd ask you about when you were born and where to start with.
I was born in Oakland, Mississippi. Which is about 65 miles south of Memphis.
Mm-hmm. And were you from a musical family at all?
You said your mother? Oh, yes. My mother was a concert pianist. My father played breakdown fiddle, hoedown fiddle, if you want to call it that. Country fiddle.

And all of my brothers played. There were four boys and we all four played. My oldest brother, Tom, never did become a professional pianist. He played nice piano, but he couldn't keep time with an eight-day alarm clock.

My next oldest brother, Johnny, Johnny Riddick, played piano in one of the finest Dixieland jazz bands in the 20s. He was six years in the Arcadia Ballroom in St. Louis. He was with the Arcadian Serenaders. The original name of the band was the Crescent City Jazzers. They originated in Mobile, Gulfport, and New Orleans. Wingy Munoon was one of the first trumpet players in that band. And Harry Tolson was one of the first clarinet players in that band, but he left that band pretty soon. And he was replaced by Cliff Holman, originally from Birmingham, Alabama. The drummer in the band just died just two years ago. Felix Guerrino, he was the original drummer in the band. He died at the age of 84 years old in Mobile. And he was originally a New Orleans boy.
I didn't know that. That somehow slipped my attention.

My brother Johnny was also born in Oakland, Mississippi. Just exactly what year. I think it was 1903. My oldest brother Tom was born in 1900. Then the next oldest brother, Dick, his name was Richard, was in 1929, acclaimed the world's greatest harmonica player in Berlin, Germany, at the Hohner harmonica factory. He had the honor of playing in the presence of President von Hindenburg in Germany in that contest. And he won that acclaim. We were both with Bora Menovic harmonica band in 1928. And we were with Helen Kane in Good Boy, the Boop Boop Be Doop Girl. Now, after that, I went to school, Spring Hill College in Mobile one year. Finished in business administration in LSU. Met my wife in April 1931 and married her in August 1931. We're still together. 52 years this coming August.
You can look at that beautiful plaque up there on the wall. It's by my niece. Her daughter made that. They are in the trophy business in Mobile, Alabama. Isn't that nice? That is. Yeah.
